source.original_question:
Catalina modeled the relationship between the number of months $T$ since she opened the restaurant and its profit $P$ (in dollars, measured as income minus expenses) as
$$
P=80(T-4)^2-300 \text {. }
$$ She wanted to create a graph to show the restaurant's profits over the first year. Here is her work: What mistakes did Catalina make when drawing the graph?
Choices:
A:Inappropriate scale for $x$-axis
B:Inappropriate scale for $y$-axis
C:Wrong/missing label for $x$-axis
D:Wrong/missing label for $y$-axis
E:Catalina didn't make any mistake

audit.source_visual_inspection: Inspected original source image before choosing the frozen mathematical model.
audit.source_observations: Original graph uses no negative y-range; gold B.)
audit.adaptation: The original criticism depends on nonstandard axes hiding negative profit, incompatible with required[-8,8] axes. Retained graph-evaluation task but redrew correctly scaled full-year profit (time/2, dollars/800); answer changes fromB toE.
